description: The Texas Citizens Participation Act: dismissal unless the plaintiff shows clear and specific evidence (In re Lipsky, Coleman, Youngkin, Adams), with defamation elements and opinion (Bentley) and due-process limits on punitive damages (Gore, State Farm v. Campbell).

name: Patent validity: invention and obviousness (1945-80)
description: Patentability before the Federal Circuit: the 'invention' requirement and combination patents (Hotchkiss, Cuno, A&P Tea, Anderson's-Black Rock, Sakraida), the Graham v. John Deere framework, and equivalence (Graver Tank).

name: Tennessee sentencing review
description: Tennessee appellate review of sentences after State v. Bise: abuse of discretion with a presumption of reasonableness for within-range sentences, extended to alternative sentencing and probation (Caudle) and consecutive sentences.

name: Illinois termination of parental rights
description: Illinois unfitness and best-interest proceedings under the Adoption and Juvenile Court Acts: clear and convincing proof of one ground of unfitness (In re D.L., In re D.D., Syck), and manifest-weight review.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Plain-error review of Booker errors (2005)
description: The 2005 circuit decisions applying Olano/Cotton plain-error review to unpreserved Booker claims: whether mandatory-Guidelines sentencing affected substantial rights (Antonakopoulos, Gonzalez-Huerta, Dazey, Dominguez Benitez).

name: Social Security exhaustion and review of agency action (1975)
description: 1975 cases on when benefits claimants may sue: § 405(g) exhaustion and final-decision requirements (Weinberger v. Salfi, Califano v. Sanders), the APA as no independent grant of jurisdiction, and veterans' benefits preclusion (Johnson v. Robison).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Federal preemption
description: When federal law displaces state law: the presumption against preemption (Rice v. Santa Fe Elevator, Lohr), express preemption (Cipollone), field and conflict preemption including obstacle preemption (Hines, Florida Avocado, Fidelity Federal v. de la Cuesta, Geier) and drug-labeling cases (Wyeth v. Levine).

name: Defamation and the First Amendment
description: New York Times v. Sullivan and its extensions: actual malice for public officials and figures (Garrison, Butts, Rosenbloom, Gertz), falsity and opinion (Hepps), and independent appellate review (Bose). Election-law cases it once absorbed sit in the ballot-access sub-clusters (21778, 19103).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Guilty pleas: voluntariness and plea bargains
description: Validity of guilty pleas: affirmative showing that a plea is knowing and voluntary (Boykin, McCarthy), the Brady v. United States trilogy, Alford pleas, enforcing plea promises (Santobello), collateral attack (Machibroda, Tollett, Timmreck) and notice of elements (Henderson v. Morgan).

name: Patent claim construction
description: Federal Circuit claim construction and infringement: Markman and de novo review (Cybor, then Teva), intrinsic evidence and the specification (Vitronics, Phillips en banc), the doctrine of equivalents and prosecution history (Warner-Jenkinson, Graver Tank) and obviousness (Graham v. John Deere).

name: Washington collateral estoppel
description: Washington Supreme Court preclusion law: issue preclusion from administrative and prior proceedings (Reninger, Nielson, Dupard, State v. Williams), with malicious prosecution and false arrest claims.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: South Dakota termination of parental rights (1985)
description: South Dakota Supreme Court parental-termination decisions turning on whether social services made sufficient reunification efforts.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Georgia capital appeals (1970s-80s)
description: Georgia Supreme Court review under the post-Gregg death-penalty statute: sentence review, prosecutorial argument that risks corrupting sentencing (Fleming), statutory aggravators in armed-robbery murders, and admissibility of statements (Ingram).

name: Pennsylvania PCRA and ineffectiveness
description: Pennsylvania post-conviction relief: ineffective-assistance claims deferred to PCRA review (Grant), the Pierce three-prong ineffectiveness test, waiver and the end of relaxed waiver in PCRA appeals, and self-representation colloquies.

name: Ohio mootness doctrine
description: Ohio courts declining to decide moot or abstract questions (Fortner, Tschantz, Cyran, Lewis), with the capable-of-repetition exception.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Kentucky criminal appeals
description: Kentucky Supreme Court criminal precedent: abuse of discretion (English), directed-verdict review (Benham), harmless error and 'fair assurance' (Winstead), and capital cases (Tamme, Stopher).

name: Summary judgment trilogy (early 1990s)
description: The 1986 summary-judgment trilogy as applied in the early 1990s: Celotex burdens, Anderson v. Liberty Lobby's reasonable-jury standard, Matsushita's 'metaphysical doubt', and inferences for the nonmovant (Diebold).

name: New Mexico civil appeals: briefing and preservation
description: New Mexico appellate rules: issues unsupported by cited authority are not reviewed (In re Adoption of Doe), summary-calendar responses must point out specific errors (Mondragon), and preservation (Self).

name: Jurisdictional versus claim-processing rules (2015)
description: The Supreme Court's sorting of deadlines and prerequisites into jurisdictional rules and nonjurisdictional claim-processing rules (Bowles, Arbaugh, Henderson v. Shinseki, Auburn Regional, Reed Elsevier v. Muchnick, Kwai Fun Wong, Gonzalez v. Thaler), with equitable tolling. Successor to the deadline thread of 26305.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: California arbitration unconscionability
description: Enforcing arbitration agreements in California: procedural and substantive unconscionability (Armendariz, Pinnacle, Sanchez, Baltazar), limited judicial review of awards (Moncharsh), class waivers after Concepcion (Discover Bank, Iskanian on PAGA) and fraud in the inducement (Engalla).

name: Illinois insurance coverage: duty to defend
description: Illinois insurance law: the insurer's duty to defend measured against the underlying complaint, ambiguities construed for the insured (Outboard Marine), and reading policies so no provision is meaningless.

name: ACCA and the categorical approach
description: Classifying prior convictions for sentencing and immigration: the categorical and modified categorical approaches (Taylor, Shepard, Descamps, Mathis), violent felonies under the Armed Career Criminal Act and its void residual clause (Begay, James, Johnson 2015), and generic offenses (Duenas-Alvarez, Moncrieffe).

name: Texas arbitration mandamus
description: Compelling arbitration in Texas by mandamus: the FAA and Texas Arbitration Act (Jack B. Anglin v. Tipps), scope and validity of the agreement (In re FirstMerit, Kellogg Brown & Root, Halliburton), and waiver by litigation conduct (In re Vesta, Bruce Terminix).

name: New Jersey civil: summary judgment and net opinions
description: New Jersey summary judgment under Brill v. Guardian Life, and the net-opinion rule excluding expert conclusions without factual or methodological support (Townsend v. Pierre, Pomerantz Paper).

name: Alabama capital appeals
description: Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals and Supreme Court review of capital convictions (Kuenzel, Bankhead, Taylor), including prosecutorial argument (United States v. Young); the parentheticals also mix in civil-contempt rulings.

name: Texas criminal: evidentiary rulings and harm analysis
description: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals evidence law: abuse-of-discretion review and Rule 403 balancing (Montgomery, Gigliobianco), extraneous offenses (De La Paz), and harm analysis for non-constitutional error under Rule 44.2(b) (King, Motilla).

name: Fourth Amendment: privacy, homes and vehicle searches
description: Expectation of privacy and standing to object (Katz, Rakas), home entry (Payton), consent (Schneckloth), the automobile exception and search incident to arrest of a vehicle (Carroll, Ross, Belton, Chimel) and the good-faith exception (Leon).

name: Sentence reductions and prisoner litigation (Fifth Circuit)
description: Fifth Circuit review of § 3582(c)(2) reductions (Dillon, Freeman) and the Fair Sentencing Act (Dorsey), together with prisoner civil-rights screening, the three-strikes rule of § 1915(g) (Adepegba, Coleman v. Tollefson) and frivolousness (Baugh).

name: First Circuit criminal appeals: waiver and sentencing
description: Sub-cluster form of the First Circuit's Zannino waiver rule for undeveloped arguments, applied with Alleyne mandatory-minimum challenges and reasonableness review of sentences (Martin, Flores-Machicote, Ruiz-Huertas).

name: Pennsylvania Rule 1925(b) waiver
description: Pennsylvania appellate waiver for issues not identified, or identified too vaguely, in a Rule 1925(b) concise statement (Lord, Castillo), with weight-of-the-evidence review.

name: California insurance coverage: duty to defend
description: California liability-insurance coverage: the broad duty to defend whenever the claim potentially falls within coverage (Gray v. Zurich, Montrose), allocation and reimbursement (Buss), interpreting policy language (AIU, Bank of the West, Waller), and pollution exclusions (MacKinnon).

name: Louisiana Anders review
description: Louisiana procedure for appointed counsel's no-merit briefs (Benjamin, Jyles, Lofton applying Anders and McCoy), errors-patent review (Oliveaux, Weiland), and Crosby pleas reserving issues.

name: Immigration: persecution and notice to appear (Tenth Circuit)
description: Tenth Circuit review of asylum and removal: past persecution and well-founded fear (Uanreroro, Sidabutar, Elzour), particular social group, and defective notices to appear and the stop-time rule after Pereira v. Sessions.

name: New York custody: best interests and nonparents
description: New York custody law: best interests and modification (Eschbach, Friederwitzer), extraordinary circumstances before a nonparent can obtain custody (Bennett v. Jeffreys), and interference with the noncustodial parent's relationship.

name: First Circuit criminal appeals: waiver of undeveloped arguments
description: First Circuit federal criminal appeals: issues adverted to in a perfunctory manner without developed argument are waived (Zannino), conspiracy and drug sentencing under the early Guidelines (David, Sepulveda), and harmless error (Kotteakos).

name: Special-needs and administrative searches
description: Fourth Amendment searches without individualized suspicion: administrative inspections (Camara), school searches (T.L.O.), drug testing (Skinner, Von Raab, Vernonia v. Acton), checkpoints (Martinez-Fuerte, Edmond), probationers (Griffin, Knights), and DNA collection (Kincade).

name: Michigan civil: summary disposition and contract
description: Michigan contract and insurance precedent: summary disposition under MCR 2.116(C)(10) (Maiden, Quinto), contracts enforced as written (Rory, Titan v. Hyten) and every word given effect (Klapp), with preservation rules.

name: Ohio civil appeals: abuse of discretion and family law
description: Ohio civil standards of review: abuse of discretion (Blakemore), competent credible evidence (C.E. Morris, Seasons Coal), Civ.R. 60(b) relief (GTE), and custody and property division in domestic-relations appeals.

name: Texas capital appeals (1970s-80s): voir dire and preservation
description: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals capital cases after 1976: excusing jurors opposed to the death penalty (Witherspoon, Adams v. Texas) and preservation (a general objection preserves nothing).

name: Nonparent custody (Illinois, D.C.)
description: Custody claims by grandparents and other nonparents: standing when a parent has relinquished physical custody (Peterson, Harne, Townsend, Carey), and the superior right of fit parents.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Labor preemption: § 301 and fair representation
description: LMRA § 301 preemption of state-law claims (Allis-Chalmers v. Lueck, Lingle), complete preemption and removal (Caterpillar, Franchise Tax Board), hybrid § 301/fair-representation suits and their limitations period (Vaca, Hines, DelCostello), and federal-question jurisdiction (Merrell Dow).

name: Tax: economic substance and assignment of income
description: Federal tax doctrines of substance over form: economic substance and sham transactions (Gregory v. Helvering, Frank Lyon, Coltec, Stobie Creek), assignment of income (Lucas v. Earl), and deductions (Welch).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Appeal deadlines, Rule 59(e) and remedies (2020)
description: 2020 sub-cluster on post-judgment procedure and equitable remedies: jurisdictional appeal deadlines and Rule 59(e) motions (Bowles, Banister, Browder, Houston v. Lack), default judgments, laches (Petrella), disgorgement as a penalty (Kokesh) and civil contempt for violating a discharge (Taggart).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Washington personal restraint petitions
description: Washington collateral review: personal restraint petitions and matters outside the record, ineffective assistance (McFarland, Thorgerson, Emery), capital review (Stenson, Pirtle), and the Frye standard for scientific evidence (Russell, Cauthron).

name: Ohio civil: summary judgment and contract interpretation
description: Ohio civil precedent on summary-judgment burdens (Dresher v. Burt, Harless, Temple), de novo review (Murphy v. Reynoldsburg), and interpreting unambiguous contracts by their plain language.

name: California Wende review and Marsden motions
description: California no-merit appeals under People v. Wende, requests to replace appointed counsel (Marsden), Three Strikes discretion (Romero, Carmony) and Pitchess discovery.

name: Collateral-order doctrine and interlocutory appeals
description: Sub-cluster form of appellate jurisdiction: Cohen's collateral-order doctrine and its narrowing (Digital Equipment, Mohawk), criminal interlocutory appeals (Abney, Flanagan, MacDonald), class-certification orders (Livesay), and mandamus (Kerr, Gulfstream).

name: Title VII procedure: EEOC charges and limitations
description: Procedural prerequisites to Title VII suits: timely EEOC charges and when discrimination accrues (Ricks, Evans), equitable tolling (Zipes, Baldwin County v. Brown), deferral to state agencies (Love, Mohasco v. Silver), § 1981 limitations (Johnson v. REA), and arbitration's non-preclusive effect (Alexander v. Gardner-Denver).

name: Mandamus and appointing counsel for indigent litigants (2005)
description: Mandamus to federal district courts (Kerr, Cheney, Roche) and whether courts may compel lawyers to represent indigent civil litigants under § 1915 (Mallard), with inherent-power sanctions (Chambers) and excusable neglect (Pioneer).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Iowa criminal appeals: error preservation and counsel
description: Iowa Supreme Court criminal precedent: issues must be both raised and decided below to be preserved (Meier v. Senecaut), ineffective-assistance claims as the route around preservation (Straw, Clay, Maxwell), and harmless hearsay.

name: Ohio criminal: pleas and felony sentencing review
description: Ohio felony sentencing after State v. Foster struck judicial fact-finding, appellate review of sentences (Kalish, then Marcum), allied offenses (Rance, Johnson), and knowing, intelligent and voluntary guilty pleas under Crim.R. 11 (Veney, Clark).

name: Zoning power and exclusionary zoning (1970s)
description: The police power to zone and its limits: Euclid and Belle Terre v. Boraas, and state-court challenges to exclusionary zoning (Mount Laurel, Girsh Appeal, National Land v. Easttown) and rent control (Inganamort). Unlike the takings sub-clusters, these ask whether zoning is valid at all.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Contract Clause
description: State laws impairing contracts: Blaisdell's emergency exception, U.S. Trust Co., Allied Structural Steel v. Spannaus, Energy Reserves Group, and federal retroactive legislation (Nachman v. PBGC).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Illinois insurance: duty to defend and pollution
description: Illinois insurance coverage: duty to defend when the complaint alleges facts potentially within coverage (Wilkin Insulation, Outboard Marine), estoppel for insurers who fail to defend (Ehlco), pollution exclusions (Koloms) and excess coverage.

name: Prisoner rights: Eighth Amendment and due process
description: Prison-conditions and prisoner civil-rights litigation: deliberate indifference to medical needs and safety (Estelle, Farmer, Wilson), conditions (Rhodes, Wolfish), disciplinary due process (Wolff, Hewitt, Sandin), access to courts (Bounds) and liberal reading of pro se pleadings (Haines, Neitzke).

name: Mens rea and mandamus (2010)
description: A small 2010 sub-cluster joining mens rea in federal crimes (Morissette, Staples, U.S. Gypsum) with mandamus to district courts (Kerr, Cheney); its mens-rea thread continues in 27704.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Preliminary injunctions and stays against the government (2025)
description: A partial 2025 sub-cluster on emergency relief: stays pending appeal (Nken, Hilton), preliminary injunctions (Winter, Sampson), APA relief (Bowen v. Massachusetts), removal of officers (Wiener, Morrison, Collins v. Yellen) and Trump v. Hawaii.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Rule 11 and inherent-power sanctions
description: Sanctions in federal litigation: Rule 11's objective standard and abuse-of-discretion review (Cooter & Gell, Business Guides, Zaldivar), sanctions on the signing attorney (Pavelic & LeFlore), inherent power (Chambers v. NASCO, Roadway Express v. Piper) and dismissal for failure to prosecute (Link).

name: California anti-SLAPP and litigation privilege
description: California's anti-SLAPP statute (Code Civ. Proc. § 425.16): protected activity and minimal merit (Equilon, Navellier, Briggs, Soukup, Baral, Park), the illegal-conduct exception (Flatley), and the litigation privilege and malicious prosecution (Silberg, Rusheen, Oren Royal Oaks).

name: Brady disclosure (2010s sub-cluster)
description: Later sub-cluster of the prosecution's disclosure duties: Brady, Giglio, Bagley materiality, Kyles' cumulative assessment and police knowledge, Strickler, and bad-faith destruction of evidence (Youngblood, Trombetta).

name: Mississippi criminal appeals (1980s-90s)
description: Mississippi Supreme Court criminal appeals: procedural bars and waiver by failure to object (Chase, Conner), admissibility of prior convictions and co-defendant statements (Hansen), and Batson race-neutral reasons (Lockett).

name: Pennsylvania suppression review and investigative stops
description: Pennsylvania suppression appeals: review limited to the suppression-hearing record (In re L.J.), reasonable suspicion and flight in high-crime areas (In re D.M.), and Vehicle Code traffic stops.

name: NLRB substantial-evidence review (1955-80)
description: Earlier sub-cluster form of NLRB law: Universal Camera's substantial-evidence standard, bargaining orders (Gissel), unilateral changes (Katz), discriminatory discharge and reinstatement remedies (Phelps Dodge, Exchange Parts).

name: Fugitive disentitlement and the Hague Abduction Convention
description: Two lines of cases on international and absconding parties: the fugitive disentitlement doctrine (Molinaro, Ortega-Rodriguez) and Hague Convention child-return cases on habitual residence, grave risk and ne exeat rights (Friedrich, Mozes, Abbott v. Abbott).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Washington subject-matter jurisdiction and finality of agency orders
description: Washington decisions distinguishing subject-matter jurisdiction from venue and other errors (Marley, Dougherty, Young), and the preclusive effect of unappealed agency orders.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: California criminal: Watson and Chapman harmless error
description: California's two harmlessness standards: Watson's reasonable-probability test for state-law error and Chapman's beyond-a-reasonable-doubt test for federal constitutional error, with Auto Equity Sales on stare decisis among California courts.

name: Foreign sovereign immunity and international law in U.S. courts
description: Suits involving foreign states and international law: the FSIA (Amerada Hess, Weltover, Nelson, Altmann), the Alien Tort Statute (Filartiga, Tel-Oren, Sosa, Kiobel), treaties and consular rights (Breard), extraterritoriality (Morrison) and the act-of-state doctrine.

name: Ballot access and election regulation (1985-95)
description: Constitutional challenges to election rules under the Anderson v. Celebrezze/Burdick balancing test: ballot access for independents and minor parties (Storer, Bullock, Williams v. Rhodes, Jenness, Munro), party primaries (Tashjian, Eu, La Follette) and candidate qualifications (Clements). Successor to the 1975 sub-cluster 19103.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Class certification under Rule 23
description: Certifying class actions: rigorous analysis of Rule 23(a) (Falcon, Wal-Mart's commonality), predominance and superiority under 23(b)(3) (Amchem, Comcast v. Behrend, Amgen), settlement classes, 23(b)(2) money claims, and due process for absent members (Shutts, Eisen).

name: Texas criminal: suppression review and traffic stops
description: Texas review of motions to suppress: almost total deference to historical facts (Guzman), de novo review of reasonable suspicion (Ford, Derichsweiler), the length of traffic-stop detentions (Kothe, Davis) and findings on request (Cullen).

name: Indian Child Welfare Act
description: ICWA in adoption and custody: domicile of Indian children (Holyfield), the 'existing Indian family' exception and its rejection (Baby Boy L., Crews, Bridget R.), and state limitations periods.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Title VII systemic and disparate-impact litigation (early 1980s)
description: Early-1980s Title VII litigation: pattern-or-practice and statistical proof (Teamsters, Hazelwood), disparate impact (Griggs, Albemarle, Dothard), McDonnell Douglas/Burdine individual claims, back pay, and clear-error review of intent (Pullman-Standard v. Swint).

name: Social Security disability review (Sixth Circuit, 1975-2000)
description: Substantial-evidence review of disability denials (Richardson v. Perales, Consolidated Edison), the medical-vocational grids (Heckler v. Campbell), and treating-physician and pain evaluation in the Sixth Circuit (Duncan, Kirk, Garner, Walters).

name: Statutory surplusage, delegation and immigration detention (2025)
description: A 2025 sub-cluster joining interpretive canons (avoid surplusage, the strongest reading: Marx, Jennings) with nondelegation (Whitman v. American Trucking), immigration detention (Zadvydas, Jennings, Biden v. Texas, Johnson v. Arteaga-Martinez) and consent-decree modification (Rufo). A partial slice; likely to settle as more years arrive.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Civil forfeiture of currency and property (1990s)
description: Federal civil forfeiture litigation: probable cause linking cash to drugs including dog alerts, and pre-seizure notice for real property (James Daniel Good).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Kansas criminal: jury instructions and clear error
description: Kansas Supreme Court criminal appeals: the multi-step analysis for jury-instruction error and clear-error review of unobjected instructions (Plummer, Williams), harmless error (Ward), and prosecutorial error.

name: Second Circuit sentencing review
description: Second Circuit review of federal sentences after Booker: Crosby remands, procedural and substantive reasonableness (Cavera en banc, Rigas, Dorvee), plain error for unpreserved sentencing objections (Villafuerte) and clear error in fact-finding.

name: Tennessee civil appeals (2020s)
description: Recent Tennessee Court of Appeals civil precedent: waiver of skeletal, undeveloped arguments (Sneed), abuse-of-discretion review in family cases (Gonsewski, Armbrister), summary judgment after Rye, and statutory construction (Lee Medical v. Beecher).

name: Judicial estoppel and preclusion
description: Barring inconsistent positions and relitigation: judicial estoppel (New Hampshire v. Maine), including in bankruptcy nondisclosure, nonparty preclusion and privity (Taylor v. Sturgell, Richards, Hansberry), federal-judgment preclusion (Semtek), and law of the case (Christianson).

name: Michigan criminal: plain error and ineffective assistance
description: Sub-cluster form of the Michigan criminal line: Carines plain error, Ginther hearings on ineffective assistance, futile objections, and other-acts evidence under MRE 404(b).

name: Wisconsin statutory interpretation
description: Wisconsin's plain-meaning method from State ex rel. Kalal (text, context and structure before legislative history), with the governor's partial veto (Citizens Utility Board, Koschkee) and agency deference ended in Tetra Tech.

name: Ohio workers' compensation mandamus
description: Ohio Supreme Court review of Industrial Commission decisions in mandamus: permanent total disability and nonmedical factors (Stephenson), the requirement to explain the evidence relied on (Noll, Mitchell), and temporary total disability (Ashcraft, Pressley).

name: Connecticut sovereign immunity and motions to dismiss
description: Connecticut precedent on subject-matter jurisdiction and immunity: colorable sovereign-immunity claims are immediately appealable (Shay v. Rossi), statutory waiver, and motions to dismiss (Gurliacci, Upson).

name: Pennsylvania discretionary aspects of sentencing
description: Pennsylvania Superior Court review of the discretionary aspects of a sentence: the substantial-question requirement, presumption that a court with a presentence report weighed mitigating factors, and excessiveness claims.

name: Wrongful birth and wrongful life
description: Tort claims by parents and children after negligent genetic counselling or prenatal diagnosis: wrongful birth recognized, wrongful life mostly rejected (Becker, Harbeson, Turpin, Berman, Procanik, Cillo, James). Successor to the wrongful-pregnancy sub-cluster 19109.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Sexual harassment under Title VII
description: Hostile-environment and quid pro quo harassment: Meritor v. Vinson, severe or pervasive conduct (Harris), same-sex harassment (Oncale), employer vicarious liability and the Faragher/Ellerth affirmative defense, and Title IX damages (Franklin v. Gwinnett).

name: False Claims Act qui tam
description: False Claims Act qui tam suits: the public-disclosure bar and original-source exception (Ninth Circuit Wang, Springfield Terminal, Stinson), state liability (Vermont Agency v. Stevens), and damages (Hess).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Oklahoma capital appeals
description: Oklahoma Court of Criminal Appeals capital cases: victim-impact evidence, the continuing-threat aggravator and remorse (Pickens), parole and commutation instructions, and Spuehler sufficiency review.

name: Exhaustion and ripeness for judicial review
description: When review of agency action is available: exhaustion of administrative remedies (Myers v. Bethlehem Shipbuilding, McKart, Weinberger v. Salfi), review despite statutory preclusion (Leedom v. Kyne, Boire, McCulloch), ripeness of rules (Abbott Laboratories, Toilet Goods) and final agency action (FTC v. Standard Oil).

name: Connecticut civil: motions to strike and negligence (sub-cluster)
description: Sub-cluster form of 1990s Connecticut civil law: motions to strike tested on the pleadings (Novametrix, Faulkner, Gordon), duty in negligence (Gazo), and negligent infliction of emotional distress in employment (Parsons).

name: Timeliness of appeals and post-judgment motions
description: When a notice of appeal is effective: timeliness as mandatory and jurisdictional (Browder, Robinson, Griggs v. Provident Consumer Discount), the prison mailbox rule (Houston v. Lack), naming parties (Torres v. Oakland Scavenger), and the effect of Rule 59(e) and 60(b) motions (Osterneck).

name: Asylum credibility and corroboration (Second Circuit)
description: Second Circuit review of asylum adverse-credibility findings: substantial evidence and deference to the IJ (Zhou Yun Zhang, Xiu Xia Lin), when corroboration may be required (Diallo), and review where the BIA summarily affirms (Secaida-Rosales).

name: Arizona termination of parental rights
description: Arizona severance proceedings: statutory grounds proved by clear and convincing evidence and best interests by a preponderance (Kent K. v. Bobby M.), appellate deference to the juvenile court (Jesus M., Mary Lou C.), and Department of Child Safety reunification efforts.

name: Securities fraud: § 10(b) scienter and pleading
description: Sub-cluster form of Rule 10b-5 doctrine: scienter (Hochfelder, Aaron, then Tellabs on pleading), materiality (TSC, Basic), deception (Santa Fe v. Green), insider trading (Chiarella), and private standing (Blue Chip Stamps, Huddleston).

name: California sexually violent predator commitments
description: California SVPA commitments: civil not punitive (Hubbart), indeterminate terms and equal protection (McKee I and II), and dangerousness evaluations (Ghilotti).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Illinois criminal: forfeiture and plain error
description: Illinois preservation rules (Enoch's contemporaneous objection plus written post-trial motion) and the two-prong plain-error doctrine for closely balanced evidence or structural error (Herron, Piatkowski, Thompson, Sebby), including jury-admonishment error under Rule 431(b) (Zehr).

name: Alabama civil: substantial evidence and workers' comp
description: Alabama civil precedent on substantial evidence (West v. Founders Life), summary judgment (Bass), workers' compensation review (Ex parte Trinity Industries), and insurance bad faith.

name: Search warrants, probable cause and the exclusionary rule
description: Warrant-based searches: probable cause from informants (Aguilar-Spinelli, then Gates' totality test), false affidavits (Franks), the good-faith exception (Leon), the scope of the exclusionary rule (Calandra, Mapp) and fruit of the poisonous tree (Wong Sun).

name: New Jersey family-court review
description: Deference to the Family Part's fact-finding (Cesare, Rova Farms) with de novo review of legal conclusions (Manalapan), in domestic-violence restraining orders (Silver) and alimony modification for changed circumstances (Lepis, Gnall, Quinn).

name: Texas civil summary judgment
description: Texas summary-judgment practice: traditional and no-evidence motions, grounds expressly presented (McConnell), the more-than-a-scintilla standard (King Ranch, Ridgway, Chapman), nonmovant burdens (Siegler), with intentional-infliction and contract issues decided on it.

name: Double jeopardy: mistrials and retrial
description: When the Double Jeopardy Clause bars a second trial: manifest necessity for mistrials (Perez, Arizona v. Washington, Somerville, Downum), defense-requested mistrials (Dinitz, Jorn), retrial after reversal for insufficiency (Burks) and government appeals (Scott).

name: Federal habeas procedure and conflicts of counsel (c. 1980)
description: Habeas doctrine around 1980: procedural default under Wainwright v. Sykes and Engle v. Isaac (replacing Fay v. Noia), deference to state findings (Sumner v. Mata), total exhaustion (Rose v. Lundy), and conflicts of interest (Holloway, Cuyler v. Sullivan).

name: ERISA benefits litigation
description: ERISA benefit-denial and fiduciary suits: Firestone v. Bruch de novo and deferential review, conflicts of interest (Glenn), treating-physician opinions (Nord), fiduciary duties (Varity v. Howe), equitable relief under § 502(a)(3) (Mertens, Great-West) and complete preemption (Davila).

name: Hawaii criminal appeals: unanimity and plain error
description: Hawaii Supreme Court criminal precedent: specific unanimity instructions for multiple acts (Arceo), plain error affecting substantial rights, and sentencing and evidence review (Kelekolio, Toyomura, Gaylord).

name: Collateral attack on deportation orders in illegal-reentry prosecutions
description: Mendoza-Lopez and due process review of the underlying deportation in § 1326 prosecutions (Proa-Tovar, Meraz-Valeta, Trevino-Martinez), joined with entrapment by estoppel (Raley, Cox v. Louisiana, PICCO).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Washington statutory interpretation (plain meaning)
description: Washington's plain-meaning rule from Department of Ecology v. Campbell & Gwinn: meaning drawn from the whole statute and related statutes, courts may not add words, and every word is given effect (J.P., Jacobs, Armendariz).

name: Pennsylvania custody and family appeals: Rule 1925(b) and relocation
description: Pennsylvania Superior Court family-law appeals: waiver under Rule 1925(b), relocation (Gruber factors), and custody evidentiary proceedings.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Tennessee post-conviction: ineffective assistance
description: Tennessee post-conviction review of counsel: the Baxter v. Rose competence standard and Strickland (Goad, Henley, Burns, Fields), failure to call witnesses, and ineffective assistance in guilty pleas (Hill v. Lockhart, Boykin).

name: Privilege against self-incrimination and immunity
description: Fifth Amendment compulsion outside custodial interrogation: use and derivative-use immunity (Kastigar, Murphy v. Waterfront Commission), public employees compelled to testify (Garrity, Gardner, Lefkowitz), the act of production (Fisher, Doe), incorporation (Malloy) and the scope of the privilege (Hoffman, Counselman).

name: Eighth Amendment categorical limits (2010)
description: Categorical Eighth Amendment protections: no death penalty for the intellectually disabled (Atkins) or juveniles (Roper), no juvenile life without parole for nonhomicide (Graham) and its 2012 sequel (Miller), proportionality (Harmelin, Solem) and Teague retroactivity.

name: Contempt: civil versus criminal
description: Distinguishing civil and criminal contempt (Gompers, Shillitani, Bagwell), jury rights for serious criminal contempt (Cheff, Bloom, Duncan, Baldwin), summary contempt and the appearance of justice (Cooke, Mayberry, Taylor v. Hayes), and obeying orders until set aside (United Mine Workers).

name: Social Security disability review (Ninth Circuit)
description: Ninth Circuit review of disability denials: substantial evidence and harmless error (Molina), weighing treating-physician opinions and the specific-and-legitimate standard (Lester, Bayliss), rejecting claimant testimony (Smolen, Tommasetti), and credit-as-true remands (Garrison).

name: Procedural due process: property, liberty and hearings
description: What process is due before government deprives a protected interest: property interests in benefits and jobs (Goldberg, Roth, Perry, Loudermill, Bishop), the Mathews v. Eldridge balancing test, notice (Mullane), parole revocation (Morrissey), prejudgment remedies (Sniadach, Fuentes) and reputation (Paul v. Davis).

name: Indiana criminal: sentence review and waiver
description: Indiana appellate review of sentences: abuse of discretion within the statutory range (Anglemyer), Appellate Rule 7(b) revision for inappropriate sentences (Cardwell, Childress), and waiver of arguments lacking cogent reasoning or citation.

name: New York land use, SEQRA and standing
description: New York Court of Appeals land-use law: environmental review under SEQRA (Jackson v. UDC, Chinese Staff & Workers), standing to challenge zoning and development (Society of Plastics, Sun-Brite), and rezoning.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Race-conscious districting and affirmative action (1990s)
description: 1990s equal protection and race: racial gerrymandering (Shaw v. Reno, Miller v. Johnson), vote dilution under the Voting Rights Act (Thornburg v. Gingles, De Grandy, Growe), and strict scrutiny of affirmative action (Croson, Adarand, Wygant, Bakke). Distinct from school desegregation (15977) and one-person-one-vote (17117).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: West Virginia abuse-and-neglect and criminal appeals
description: West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals precedent on child abuse and neglect proceedings (improvement periods, clearly-erroneous review in In re Tiffany Marie S.) and collateral-crimes evidence in child sexual assault cases (Edward Charles L.).

name: Wisconsin criminal appeals: undeveloped arguments and counsel
description: Wisconsin appellate practice: undeveloped or inadequately briefed arguments are not addressed (Pettit), Machner hearings and ineffective assistance with aggregated prejudice (Thiel), postconviction motions (Allen, Bentley, Balliette) and sufficiency (Poellinger).

name: Federal jurisdiction over welfare and constitutional claims (1955-80)
description: 1960s-70s suits challenging state welfare rules (King v. Smith, Rosado): the insubstantiality doctrine for federal jurisdiction (Hagans, Poresky, Goosby), three-judge courts, and pendent jurisdiction over state-law claims (Gibbs).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Batson: discriminatory jury strikes
description: Equal protection limits on peremptory challenges: Batson's three-step framework, race-neutral explanations (Purkett, Hernandez), third-party standing (Powers), defense strikes (McCollum), gender (J.E.B.), and comparative juror analysis (Miller-El 2005, Snyder). Succeeded Swain v. Alabama.

name: Personal jurisdiction (sub-cluster)
description: Sub-cluster form of the minimum-contacts line: International Shoe, Hanson v. Denckla, McGee, World-Wide Volkswagen, Keeton, Burger King, Asahi and Helicopteros, plus Shaffer's extension to quasi in rem jurisdiction.

name: Eleventh Amendment: state sovereign immunity and Ex parte Young
description: States' immunity from suit in federal court as settled from the 1980s: Hans, Pennhurst on state-law claims, Seminole Tribe and Alden limiting Congress's power to abrogate, waiver (College Savings Bank), and the Ex parte Young route to prospective relief. Its 1970s predecessor (18304) mixed this with federal power over state employees.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Wrongful pregnancy after failed sterilization
description: Damages when a negligent sterilization leads to a healthy child: whether child-rearing costs are recoverable (Troppi, Sherlock, Custodio, Coleman, Rieck, Ochs). Predecessor of the wrongful-birth sub-cluster 21878.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Texas criminal: jury-charge error and egregious harm
description: Texas review of jury-charge error under Almanza: some harm for preserved error and egregious harm for unpreserved error (Hutch, Ngo), lesser-included offenses and defensive instructions.

name: Tennessee termination of parental rights
description: Tennessee parental-termination law: grounds and best interest proved by clear and convincing evidence (In re Valentine, Audrey S., Carrington H.), substantial noncompliance with a permanency plan, and constitutional protection of the family (Stanley, Santosky).

name: Employment discrimination: McDonnell Douglas pretext
description: Individual disparate-treatment claims under Title VII and the ADEA: the McDonnell Douglas/Burdine/Hicks framework, pretext (Reeves), retaliation (Burlington Northern v. White), hostile environment (Harris), mixed motive and but-for causation (Price Waterhouse), decided on summary judgment.

name: State action: private actors under § 1983 (2020)
description: When private parties act under color of state law: Lugar, Blum v. Yaretsky, Rendell-Baker, Brentwood Academy's entwinement test, contract prison physicians (West v. Atkins) and Manhattan Community Access v. Halleck.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Federal conspiracy and variance (c. 1970)
description: Federal conspiracy prosecutions: variance between indictment and proof (Kotteakos, Stirone), Pinkerton liability, aiding and abetting (Nye & Nissen, Pereira), and corroboration of confessions (Opper).

name: Booker remands (2005)
description: The 2005 wave of federal appeals sorting out Booker error: whether a sentence imposed under mandatory Guidelines requires resentencing, plain-error treatment of unpreserved claims, and § 3582(c)(2) reductions.

name: Ohio custody and dependency appeals
description: Ohio parental-rights and custody review: the parent's fundamental interest in custody (In re Murray, In re Hayes), manifest-weight review in civil cases (Eastley), and deference to the trial court's observation of witnesses (Seasons Coal).

name: Freedom of Information Act exemptions
description: FOIA litigation over agency withholding: Exemption 2 (Rose), privacy under Exemptions 6 and 7(C) and the public-interest balance (Reporters Committee), deliberative-process privilege (Sears, Coastal States, Klamath), segregability (Mead Data), Vaughn indexes and adequate searches (Oglesby, Safecard, Morley); D.C. Circuit heavy.

name: New Jersey administrative-agency review
description: New Jersey appellate review of agency decisions: affirmance unless arbitrary, capricious or unreasonable or unsupported by substantial credible evidence (In re Stallworth, Herrmann, Carter), with deference to agency expertise (Mayflower Securities).

name: Texas mandamus
description: Original mandamus proceedings in Texas: clear abuse of discretion and no adequate remedy by appeal (Walker v. Packer, In re Prudential), ministerial duties to rule on motions, new-trial orders (Johnson v. Fourth Court of Appeals, Columbia Medical), and discovery and forum orders.

name: New York contract and commercial claims
description: New York commercial litigation on motions to dismiss (Leon v. Martinez, Guggenheimer): quasi-contract barred by a valid written contract, the implied covenant (Murphy v. American Home Products), fraud and puffery (Wildenstein), and General Business Law § 349 territoriality (Goshen).

name: Washington insurance: bad faith and duty to defend
description: Washington insurance law: attorney's fees for insureds who must sue for coverage (Olympic Steamship), bad faith and the duty to defend (Kirk, Truck Insurance Exchange v. VanPort Homes, Safeco v. Butler), and reservation-of-rights defenses (Tank).

name: Washington family-law appeals
description: Washington dissolution and parenting appeals: the trial court's broad discretion over parenting plans and relocation (Littlefield, Katare), property division and retirement benefits (Bulicek, Muhammad), and waiver of issues raised only in a reply brief (Bosley).

name: Right to counsel: self-representation and conflicts
description: Sixth Amendment counsel rights: self-representation and standby counsel (Faretta, McKaskle), counsel of choice (Gonzalez-Lopez), conflicts of interest (Cuyler v. Sullivan), competency (Dusky), and structural error (Fulminante, Tumey).

name: Texas statutory construction and agency deference
description: Texas courts reading statutes: legislative intent, presumed knowledge of existing law, avoiding absurd results, and deference to the agency charged with enforcement (Fitzgerald, Rylander, City of San Antonio v. Boerne), with DTPA coverage and immunity waivers.

name: Mens rea and federal criminal statutes
description: Reading knowledge requirements into federal crimes: Morissette, Staples, X-Citement Video, Flores-Figueroa, Liparota, U.S. Gypsum and Cheek (willfulness), against regulatory public-welfare offenses (Freed). Distinct from the 2010 mandamus-and-mens-rea mix 26996.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: RICO
description: The Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act: what counts as an enterprise (Turkette), private civil RICO without a prior conviction (Sedima), the pattern requirement of continuity plus relationship (H.J. Inc.), and operation-or-management liability (Reves).

name: Speedy trial (sub-cluster)
description: Sub-cluster form of the speedy-trial line: Barker v. Wingo's four factors, Doggett, pre-indictment delay (Marion, Lovasco), incorporation against the states (Klopfer), applied heavily by Texas courts.

name: Second Amendment
description: The individual right to keep and bear arms: Heller, its incorporation (McDonald), the circuits' two-step intermediate-scrutiny framework (Heller II, Marzzarella, Chester, Skoien, Ezell), and its replacement by Bruen's text-and-history test (and Rahimi).

name: New Mexico criminal appeals: double jeopardy and evidence
description: New Mexico appellate criminal precedent: multiple punishment and unitary conduct (Swafford, Montoya), the jury's freedom to reject a defendant's account (Sutphin, Rojo), preservation, and harmless error (Tollardo).

name: North Carolina capital appeals: proportionality review
description: North Carolina Supreme Court capital appeals: statutory proportionality review comparing similar cases ('robbery-murder'), aggravating and mitigating circumstance instructions (Artis), and preservation of constitutional issues (Benson).

name: Confrontation Clause after Crawford
description: Testimonial hearsay and the right to cross-examine: Crawford, Davis/Hammon's ongoing-emergency test, Michigan v. Bryant, forensic reports (Melendez-Diaz, Bullcoming, Williams v. Illinois), with the earlier Ohio v. Roberts, Bruton and Van Arsdall.

name: Disability discrimination: ADA and Rehabilitation Act
description: What counts as a disability and what employers owe: substantial limitation of a major life activity (Sutton, Murphy, Kirkingburg, Toyota v. Williams, Bragdon), reasonable accommodation, and Rehabilitation Act § 504 (Arline, Southeastern Community College v. Davis, Alexander v. Choate).

name: Colorado criminal: equal protection and overlapping statutes
description: Colorado Supreme Court decisions holding criminal statutes unconstitutional where they punish identical conduct differently (Calvaresi, Marcy on extreme-indifference murder) and deadly-weapon definitions.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Florida capital postconviction and Hurst
description: Florida death-penalty litigation: Rule 3.851 postconviction claims and Huff hearings, strategic decisions of counsel (Occhicone, Sochor), and Hurst v. Florida's application of Ring to Florida's sentencing scheme.

name: Brady disclosure and false testimony
description: The prosecution's due-process duties: suppression of exculpatory and impeachment evidence (Brady, Giglio, Agurs, Bagley, Kyles, Strickler), knowing use of false testimony (Mooney, Napue) and failure to preserve evidence (Trombetta, Youngblood).

name: Washington post-conviction ineffective assistance
description: Washington personal restraint petitions on ineffective assistance: Strickland as applied in Grier (all-or-nothing strategy), McFarland, Kyllo, reference hearings for factual disputes, and failure to propose instructions.

name: Takings Clause: regulatory and physical takings (1980 on)
description: Modern takings law: Penn Central balancing, categorical takings (Loretto physical occupation, Lucas total wipeout), exactions (Nollan, Dolan), Agins and its rejection in Lingle, and ripeness (Williamson County). Its 1970s predecessor (18309) was built on Mahon's 'too far' test.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: ERISA preemption
description: ERISA § 514 preemption of state law: 'relate to' an employee benefit plan (Shaw, Ingersoll-Rand, Travelers), the savings clause and insurance regulation (Metropolitan Life v. Massachusetts, FMC v. Holliday), exclusive civil enforcement (Pilot Life v. Dedeaux, Taylor) and what counts as a plan (Fort Halifax).

name: Texas civil: sufficiency, damages and expert causation
description: Texas Supreme Court review of jury findings: legal and factual sufficiency, the jury as sole judge of credibility, expert reliability and toxic-tort causation (Robinson, Havner), exemplary damages (Moriel) and attorney's fees.

name: Vagueness and overbreadth challenges to criminal laws
description: Facial challenges to criminal statutes and ordinances as void for vagueness or overbroad: Kolender, Chicago v. Morales loitering, Hoffman Estates, Grayned, Ferber and child pornography, Salerno's no-set-of-circumstances test, with Texas Court of Criminal Appeals decisions (Ely, Long, Santikos). Narrower and more criminal than the general speech sub-cluster 13116.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Illinois postconviction petitions
description: The Illinois Post-Conviction Hearing Act: first-stage summary dismissal of frivolous or patently meritless petitions (Hodges, Edwards), supporting affidavits (Coleman, Collins), and postconviction counsel's Rule 651(c) duties (Pendleton, Addison).

name: Selective prosecution (1975)
description: Selective-enforcement claims: Yick Wo, Oyler v. Boles, and the 1970s circuit tests for discriminatory prosecution (Berrios, Falk, Steele, Berrigan).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Ohio criminal: sufficiency versus manifest weight
description: Sub-cluster form of the Ohio line distinguishing sufficiency (Jenks) from manifest weight of the evidence (Thompkins, Martin), with Tibbs v. Florida on why a weight reversal does not bar retrial, and Bradley ineffective assistance.

name: Asylum: persecution and social group (Eighth and other circuits)
description: Circuit review of asylum claims: persecution and economic harm (Matter of Acosta), political opinion and particular social group, past persecution and presumptions, and the Elias-Zacarias compelled-to-conclude standard.

name: Civil-rights attorney's fees (§ 1988)
description: Sub-cluster form of fee-shifting: prevailing-party status (Hewitt, Farrar, Texas Teachers, Maher), the lodestar and its adjustments (Hensley, Blum, Johnson v. Georgia Highway Express, Delaware Valley), and the American Rule (Alyeska).

name: Texas sovereign and governmental immunity
description: Texas immunity from suit for the State and local governments: pleas to the jurisdiction (Miranda, Blue, Texas Ass'n of Business), waiver only by clear legislative language (Tooke, IT-Davy, Little-Tex), the Tort Claims Act, and the ultra vires exception (Heinrich).

name: Juvenile justice due process (1960s-70s)
description: Constitutionalizing juvenile proceedings: waiver hearings (Kent), notice, counsel and confrontation (In re Gault), proof beyond a reasonable doubt (Winship), no jury right (McKeiver), with sentencing due process (Townsend, Williams v. New York, Specht).

name: Nebraska juvenile and termination appeals
description: Nebraska Supreme Court juvenile proceedings: final dispositional orders and appeal deadlines, rehabilitation plans and termination of parental rights.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Joint trials, conspiracy and severance
description: Federal joint trials of co-conspirators: severance and antagonistic defenses (Zafiro), Bruton limits on co-defendant confessions, co-conspirator statements (Bourjaily), Pinkerton liability, and Fifth Circuit en banc law (Calverley, Beechum).

name: Pennsylvania standing, ripeness and single-subject challenges
description: Pennsylvania Supreme Court doctrines on who may sue and when: aggrieved-party standing (Wm. Penn Parking Garage, Fumo, Stilp), advisory opinions and ripeness, and single-subject challenges to legislation.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Judicial review of agency action: deference and reasoned decision-making
description: How courts review agencies: deference to agency interpretations (Chevron and its limits in Mead, Christensen and Brown & Williamson; Skidmore weight; Auer/Seminole Rock for an agency's own regulations; Brand X), and the arbitrary-and-capricious requirement of reasoned decision-making (State Farm, Overton Park), with NEPA review (Marsh).
edited: 2026-10-01: renamed after reviewing the State Farm note (label was narrower than the cluster)

name: Tennessee divorce: alimony, property and parenting
description: Tennessee family law: classification and division of marital property including retirement benefits (Cohen, Batson), types of alimony (Burlew, Crabtree, Gonsewski), and modification of parenting schedules on a material change in circumstances.

name: Public trial and press access to proceedings
description: Openness of criminal proceedings: the First Amendment right of access (Richmond Newspapers, Globe Newspaper, Press-Enterprise I and II), the Sixth Amendment public-trial right and closure findings (Waller, Washington's Bone-Club factors), and the common-law right to judicial records (Nixon v. Warner Communications).

name: Federal habeas: AEDPA deference and procedural default
description: Federal collateral review under AEDPA: unreasonable application of clearly established law (Williams v. Taylor, Harrington, Pinholster), procedural default and cause (Coleman, Murray v. Carrier), certificates of appealability (Slack, Miller-El), Brecht harmlessness, and Strickland/Wiggins and Brady/Kyles claims.

name: Eyewitness identification and lineups
description: Pretrial identification: the right to counsel at post-indictment lineups (Wade, Gilbert, Kirby), suggestive procedures and due process (Stovall, Simmons, Foster), and reliability under Neil v. Biggers and Manson v. Brathwaite.

name: Apprendi: jury findings and the statutory maximum
description: The immediate Apprendi wave: facts increasing a penalty beyond the statutory maximum must go to a jury, the prior-conviction exception (Almendarez-Torres), and plain-error and harmless-error treatment of Apprendi errors (Johnson, Neder, Cotton, Olano).

name: Equal protection: rational-basis review
description: The deferential tier of equal protection: economic and social-welfare classifications upheld if any rational basis exists (Williamson v. Lee Optical, McGowan, Dandridge, Lindsley, Fritz), age (Murgia), education funding (Rodriguez), durational residency and travel (Shapiro, Dunn). Contrast 19102, the intermediate-scrutiny classifications (sex, legitimacy).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Massachusetts employment: at-will and implied covenant
description: Massachusetts at-will employment: the public-policy exception and the implied covenant of good faith (Fortune line, Gram, Wright v. Shriners, Jackson v. ABCD), decided on summary judgment (Dawes, Kourouvacilis).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Washington torts: government duty and the CPA
description: Washington tort precedent on public entities' duties: take-charge duties of parole and probation officers (Taggart, Hertog), the public-duty doctrine (Taylor), and Consumer Protection Act claims (Hangman Ridge elements, Bain on deeds of trust).

name: California sentencing reform and resentencing (2020s)
description: California's 2018-2022 sentencing changes: retroactive ameliorative statutes under In re Estrada, discretion to strike enhancements (Romero, Carmony), ability to pay fines (Dueñas), and youth-offender issues after Miller (Gutierrez).

name: Mootness and vacatur (1970)
description: Mootness doctrine around 1970: voluntary cessation (W.T. Grant), capable of repetition (Southern Pacific Terminal, Moore v. Ogilvie), partial mootness (Powell v. McCormack), and vacating judgments of moot cases (Munsingwear).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Feres doctrine and Bivens remedies
description: Limits on suing the United States and its officers: the Feres bar on service-related claims under the FTCA (Brooks, Brown, Stencel, Shearer) and its Bivens counterpart (Chappell, Stanley), prisoner FTCA claims (Muniz), Bivens and its alternatives (Carlson, Bush v. Lucas, Schweiker v. Chilicky).

name: Harmless error and structural error (1995)
description: Mid-1990s harmless-error doctrine: Chapman's beyond-reasonable-doubt test, Brecht and Kotteakos on collateral review, structural errors like a defective reasonable-doubt instruction (Sullivan v. Louisiana) and denial of counsel (Gideon, Faretta), and Fulminante.

name: Louisiana civil: insurance interpretation and malpractice
description: Louisiana civil precedent: insurance policies construed by plain meaning and ambiguities against the insurer (Reynolds v. Select Properties), summary judgment (Schroeder, Samaha) and medical malpractice causation.

name: Illinois constitutional challenges and substantive due process (2025)
description: A partial 2025 sub-cluster of Illinois Supreme Court cases on constitutional challenges to statutes and fines (Jones, Napleton, Boeckmann), with Glucksberg and Albright v. Oliver.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Statutes of repose for builders and architects
description: State-court challenges to statutes of repose protecting architects and builders from claims arising from improvements to real property (Rosenberg, Freezer Storage, Skinner, Kallas Millwork, Klein): due process, equal protection and open-courts arguments.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Eleventh Circuit: adopting former Fifth Circuit precedent
description: Early Eleventh Circuit criminal appeals (1980s) whose common thread is Bonner v. City of Prichard: decisions of the former Fifth Circuit handed down before October 1, 1981 are binding precedent in the Eleventh Circuit; with extrinsic-act evidence (Beechum) and indictments (Hamling).

name: Habeas timeliness and equitable tolling
description: AEDPA's one-year limitations period: equitable tolling for extraordinary circumstances (Holland, Pace, Rose v. Lee), actual-innocence gateways (Schlup), second or successive petitions (Slack, Gonzalez v. Crosby) and certificates of appealability (Miller-El); Fourth Circuit heavy.

name: Louisiana prescription and asbestos claims
description: Louisiana prescription (statutes of limitation) and contra non valentem (Corsey, Carter, Campo), asbestos exposure and causation, insurance trigger (Cole v. Celotex), and limits on retroactive legislation.

name: Oregon statutory interpretation
description: Oregon's interpretive method: PGE's text-and-context first level, modified by State v. Gaines to allow legislative history, the court's duty to find the correct interpretation (Stull), and avoiding surplusage (Cloutier).

name: New York premises liability
description: New York negligence on summary judgment: actual and constructive notice of a dangerous condition (Gordon v. American Museum, Piacquadio), contractors' duties to third parties (Espinal), intervening causes (Derdiarian), and the Alvarez/Winegrad/Zuckerman burdens.

name: Texas parental-rights termination
description: Termination of parental rights in Texas: statutory endangerment grounds under § 161.001(1), the Holley best-interest factors, clear-and-convincing evidence and heightened sufficiency review (In re C.H., In re J.F.C.), and incarceration as endangerment (Boyd).

name: Texas default judgments and restricted appeals
description: Setting aside default judgments in Texas under Craddock v. Sunshine Bus Lines (no conscious indifference, meritorious defense, no undue delay), lack of notice (Peralta), defective service, bills of review and restricted appeals.

name: Florida divorce: equitable distribution and alimony
description: Florida domestic-relations law: equitable distribution and lump-sum alimony (Canakaris, including its abuse-of-discretion test), competent substantial evidence (Shaw v. Shaw), and attorney's fee lodestar findings (Florida Patient's Compensation Fund v. Rowe).

name: Double jeopardy: same offense and multiple punishment
description: The Double Jeopardy Clause: Blockburger's same-elements test, multiple punishments and legislative intent (Whalen, Albernaz, Missouri v. Hunter), successive prosecutions (Brown v. Ohio, Grady, Dixon), collateral estoppel (Ashe), incorporation (Benton) and vindictive resentencing (Pearce).

name: Qualified immunity and § 1983 officer liability
description: Suits against officials under § 1983 from Monroe v. Pape onward: qualified immunity and clearly established law (Harlow, Anderson v. Creighton, Pearson, Hope), interlocutory appeal of its denial (Forsyth, Johnson v. Jones), excessive and deadly force (Graham, Scott v. Harris) and municipal liability (Monell).

name: Right to appointed counsel (1970s)
description: The right to counsel after Gideon: misdemeanors with imprisonment (Argersinger, Scott v. Illinois), waiver (Zerbst, Carnley), self-representation (Faretta), uncounseled prior convictions (Burgett, Loper), and denial of consultation during an overnight recess (Geders).

name: Texas Anders briefs (1990s-2000s)
description: Anders and Penson as applied in Texas: what an Anders brief must contain (High, Currie, Stafford), the appellate court's independent review (Bledsoe), and notice-of-appeal limits on what can be raised.

name: Party presentation, Erie and the Rules Enabling Act (2020s)
description: Recent cases on what courts may decide and which law applies: the party-presentation principle (Greenlaw, Sineneng-Smith), Erie, Hanna and Shady Grove, extraterritoriality (Morrison, Aramco), and recharacterizing filings (Castro).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Federal Indian law and tribal sovereignty
description: Tribal sovereignty and state authority in Indian country: Worcester v. Georgia, infringement of tribal self-government (Williams v. Lee), state taxation (McClanahan, Moe, Colville, Bracker), tribal jurisdiction over nonmembers (Montana, Oliphant), sovereign immunity and ICRA (Santa Clara Pueblo, Wheeler).

name: Ohio postconviction relief and res judicata
description: Ohio's bar on relitigating in postconviction proceedings claims that could have been raised on direct appeal (State v. Perry, Cole), postconviction petitions (Calhoun), and resentencing for post-release control (Bezak, Fischer).

name: Eleventh Circuit sentencing reasonableness
description: Eleventh Circuit review of federal sentences after Booker: substantive reasonableness (Talley, Pugh, Irey en banc), within-range sentences as indicators of reasonableness, and the Bonner v. City of Prichard rule adopting pre-October 1981 Fifth Circuit decisions as binding.

name: California capital appeals
description: California Supreme Court review of death judgments: Ring's jury-finding requirement for aggravating circumstances and the state court's repeated rejection of challenges to California's death-penalty statute, with Watson harmlessness.

name: Texas criminal: ineffective assistance on direct appeal
description: Strickland as applied by the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals: a silent record on direct appeal rarely shows deficient performance (Thompson, Bone, Goodspeed, Mallett), so counsel's conduct is presumed strategic unless it was so outrageous no competent attorney would engage in it.

name: Commerce power: Lopez, Morrison and federal crimes
description: Limits on Congress's commerce power (Lopez, Morrison, measured against Wickard, Perez and Heart of Atlanta) as applied to federal criminal statutes with jurisdictional elements (Jones v. United States arson, Bass, Scarborough, Russell). Unlike 26995, which joins commerce power to sex-offender registration, this one is about the statutes' reach.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Chapter 15 bankruptcy and international comity
description: Cross-border insolvency: recognition of foreign proceedings under Chapter 15 and center of main interests (SPhinX, Tri-Continental, Atlas Shipping), comity to foreign judgments (Hilton v. Guyot) and non-debtor injunctions.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Sufficiency review in Georgia and Louisiana criminal appeals
description: Jackson v. Virginia sufficiency as applied by Georgia and Louisiana courts: the jury resolves conflicts and judges credibility, and the appellate court asks only whether any rational trier of fact could find the elements proved.

name: Antitrust: Sherman Act restraints and antitrust injury
description: Sherman and Clayton Act doctrine: per se rules versus the rule of reason (Socony-Vacuum, Board of Trade, Topco, Professional Engineers), vertical restraints (Schwinn, Continental T.V., Monsanto), tying (Northern Pacific, Jefferson Parish v. Hyde), intra-enterprise conspiracy (Copperweld) and antitrust injury (Brunswick, AGC v. Carpenters).

name: Article III standing
description: Standing doctrine: injury in fact, traceability and redressability (Lujan, Warth, Allen, Simon), taxpayer and organizational standing (Valley Forge, Havens), future injury and injunctions (Lyons, Clapper's 'certainly impending'), environmental plaintiffs (Friends of the Earth, Steel Co.) and concreteness (Spokeo).

name: New York criminal appeals: weight, preservation, counsel
description: Sub-cluster form of the New York Court of Appeals criminal line: weight-of-the-evidence review (Bleakley, Danielson), the specific-objection preservation rule for sufficiency (Gray, Hawkins) and meaningful representation (Baldi, Benevento).

name: Labor arbitration: Steelworkers Trilogy
description: Arbitration under collective-bargaining agreements: the Steelworkers Trilogy, § 301 enforcement (Lincoln Mills), procedural arbitrability for arbitrators (Wiley v. Livingston), no-strike injunctions (Boys Markets) and deference to awards (Misco, W.R. Grace).

name: Plain error and new rules on direct review (1995)
description: Rule 52(b) after Olano: plain error judged at the time of appeal when the law changes (Johnson v. United States after Gaudin's materiality-to-the-jury rule), new rules on direct review (Griffith), and inconsistent verdicts.

name: Dormant Commerce Clause
description: State laws burdening interstate commerce: discrimination and economic protectionism (Philadelphia v. New Jersey, Hughes, Oregon Waste, Carbone v. Clarkstown), the Pike balancing test, state taxes (Complete Auto v. Brady, Bacchus, Limbach) and the market-participant line (Exxon v. Maryland).

name: Mississippi divorce: equitable distribution and custody
description: Mississippi domestic-relations law: equitable distribution under the Ferguson factors and classification of marital assets (Hemsley), alimony after division (Armstrong, Johnson v. Johnson), grounds for divorce, and the Albright custody factors.

name: California privacy and Unruh Act (1975-85)
description: California's constitutional right of privacy against compelled disclosure (Lifschutz, White v. Davis, Valley Bank, Britt) and the Unruh Civil Rights Act.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: New York no-fault serious injury
description: Summary judgment on 'serious injury' under New York Insurance Law § 5102(d): objective proof of significant limitation (Toure, Licari, Gaddy), gaps in treatment and preexisting conditions (Pommells, Perl), and admissible medical reports (Grasso).

name: California civil appeals and the Bane Act
description: California appellate presumptions (Denham's presumption of correctness, Jameson on the record), relief from default (Rappleyea), and Bane Act civil-rights claims requiring coercion and specific intent.

name: Patent obviousness and PTAB review
description: Obviousness under § 103 after KSR (Graham factors, motivation to combine, hindsight), Federal Circuit substantial-evidence review of PTAB and examiner fact-finding (Gartside, Nuvasive, Intelligent Bio-Systems), and inter partes review (SAS Institute v. Iancu).

name: Arizona criminal appeals: fundamental error and capital review
description: Arizona Supreme Court criminal precedent: fundamental-error review of unobjected-to error (Henderson), Anders/Leon full-record review, and capital-case issues (Gretzler, Bible's Frye ruling, Atwood).

name: Mandamus, supplemental jurisdiction and federal-court power
description: Supervisory mandamus over district courts (Roche, La Buy, Schlagenhauf, Will, Kerr), review of remand orders (Thermtron v. Hermansdorfer), the amount in controversy (St. Paul Mercury, Zahn), and supplemental jurisdiction after dismissing federal claims (Gibbs, Cohill).

name: Class actions, standing and immunity in challenges to government (2025)
description: A partial 2025 sub-cluster of suits challenging government programs: class certification (Wal-Mart, Falcon, Califano v. Yamasaki), standing (Lewis v. Casey, Hollingsworth, Kowalski), Ex parte Young, presidential power (Youngstown) and Plyler. Likely to settle as the slice fills.
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Asylum: persecution and nexus (Ninth Circuit)
description: Circuit review of asylum denials, mainly in the Ninth Circuit: persecution on account of a protected ground and nexus (Elias-Zacarias), well-founded fear (Cardoza-Fonseca, Stevic), corroboration after the REAL ID Act, and remand to the agency (INS v. Ventura).

name: New Jersey criminal sentencing and trial error
description: New Jersey criminal precedent: sentencing review of aggravating and mitigating factors (State v. Roth, Fuentes, Case), consecutive sentences (Yarbough), prosecutorial summation (Frost), and cumulative error (Weaver).

name: Copyright: originality, infringement and fair use
description: Copyright law: originality (Feist), idea versus expression (Baker v. Selden, Computer Associates v. Altai), fair use (Sony, Harper & Row, Campbell v. Acuff-Rose), derivative works (Stewart v. Abend), fee awards (Fogerty), and online secondary liability (Perfect 10).

name: Connecticut termination of parental rights
description: Connecticut child-protection appeals: termination grounds and reunification efforts (In re Eden F., In re Luis C., In re Juvenile Appeal decisions), family integrity, and prenatal conduct (In re Valerie D.).
written_by: claude (Cowork session, contrastive pass from family evidence)

name: Massachusetts civil: summary judgment and implied covenant
description: Massachusetts summary-judgment burdens (Kourouvacilis, Pederson), the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing (Anthony's Pier Four), and premises and negligence duties (Mullins).

name: Virginia Court of Appeals criminal review
description: Virginia criminal appeals: deciding on the best and narrowest grounds, sufficiency and the reasonable-hypothesis-of-innocence rule for circumstantial evidence (Haskins, Higginbotham), viewing the whole record (Bolden), and hearsay exceptions (Martin).

name: California civil: employment, premises duty and summary judgment
description: California civil precedent: summary judgment (Aguilar), FEHA discrimination and retaliation (Guz, Yanowitz, Harris v. Santa Monica), and the duty and foreseeability analysis for premises liability (Rowland, Ann M., Saelzler).

name: Medical-malpractice tort reform challenges (1975-80)
description: Constitutional challenges to 1970s medical-malpractice reforms: pre-trial screening panels and the jury right (Eastin, Prendergast, Paro, Attorney General v. Johnson) and damages caps (Wright v. Central Du Page).

name: Civil forfeiture, double jeopardy and excessive fines
description: Whether civil sanctions are punishment: civil penalties and forfeitures under the Double Jeopardy Clause (Halper, Kurth Ranch, Ursery, Hudson), forfeiture under the Excessive Fines Clause (Austin), and innocent-owner forfeiture (Calero-Toledo).
